newsitem.title: UK: Anagen rejects liquidator, eyes refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Anagen rejects liquidator, eyes refinancing.

text.p: British diagnostics group Anagen Plc said on Wednesday it had rejected a resolution to appoint a liquidator for the firm following a refinancing proposal put forward by a private investor.
Anagen said the planned refinancing would involve an injection of capital via debt and an issue of equity.
Details would be announced "in due course'.
Trading in Anagen's shares was suspended in September 1996, after talks with two potential marketing partners for its AuraFlex diagnostic system collapsed.
In December, Anagen disposed of its AuraFlex system to Alfa-Biotech SpA., a division of the Alfa-Wasserman group.
Liquidators Arthur Andersen had advised Anagen that it should wind up its affairs as funds arising from the disposal were not enough for it to continue trade.
